overview.title: Welcome to Laâyoune — Where the Desert Meets the Atlantic
overview.p1: Laâyoune is the largest city and economic heart of the Moroccan Sahara. Situated on the dry bed of the Saguia el-Hamra river and just 25 kilometers from the Atlantic shore, it bridges modern urban development with centuries-old nomadic customs.
overview.p2: From traditional three-round Sahrawi tea ceremonies to fresh seafood catches at the port of El Marsa and peaceful ocean sunsets at Foum El Oued beach, Laâyoune offers an authentic southern desert experience.

places.title: Must-Visit Places in Laâyoune
places.subtitle: Monuments, Atlantic beaches, desert oases, and vibrant local markets.

jemaa.title: Place Mechouar
jemaa.desc: The landmark monumental square lined with palatial Sahrawi gates and lush gardens.

majorelle.title: Foum El Oued Beach
majorelle.desc: A long expanse of Atlantic sandy coastline ideal for seaside walks and fresh air.

bahia.title: El Marsa Port
bahia.desc: Bustling fishing port known for daily ocean catches and grilled sardines.

ben_youssef.title: Saguia el-Hamra
ben_youssef.desc: Historic river valley oasis featuring date palm groves and surrounding desert landscapes.

saadian.title: Souk Soune
saadian.desc: Traditional bazaar with Sahrawi silver crafts, camel leather goods, and colorful melhfa fabrics.

elbadi.title: Spanish Quarter & Cathedral
elbadi.desc: Historic colonial architecture standing in contrast with modern desert buildings.

jardin_menara.title: Moulay Abdellah Mosque
jardin_menara.desc: An emblem of Islamic architecture with modern Sahrawi decorative touches.

dar_el_bacha.title: Lemsid Dune Sea
dar_el_bacha.desc: Majestic golden sand dunes on the outskirts of the city ideal for sunset watching.

koutoubia.title: Place Oulad Tedrarag
koutoubia.desc: Lush palm park providing cool shade and evening family promenades.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A balanced plan to discover the city landmarks, the port, and the surrounding desert.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Stroll around Place Mechouar, admiring the Sahrawi architectural motifs and broad palm-lined boulevards.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Browse traditional silver jewelry, camel-leather goods, and colorful melhfa fabrics in local markets.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Experience local tea hospitality (Atay) served in three distinct rounds in a relaxed city café.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Head west to the port town of El Marsa to observe fishing boats returning with the daily Atlantic catch.
detailed_itinerary.day2_a: Afternoon — Foum El Oued Ocean Relax
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Enjoy lunch with freshly grilled fish, then unwind along the wide sandy beach of Foum El Oued.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Watch the sunset as the golden desert dunes merge directly into the ocean shore.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Explore the palm groves and dry river bed landscapes north-east of Laâyoune.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Take a short camel trek across the golden dunes surrounding the city limits.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Enjoy camel meat tagine or fresh grilled sea bass in one of Laâyoune's authentic local restaurants.

eat.title: Best Restaurants & Cafés
eat.subtitle: Fresh Atlantic seafood, grilled meats, and local tea spots.

nomad.title: El Marsa Port Grills
nomad.desc: Savor freshly caught Atlantic fish and sardines grilled right beside the harbor.

jardin.title: Traditional Tagine House
jardin.desc: Famous for slow-cooked camel meat tagines served with local flatbreads.

fassia.title: Mechouar Avenue Cafés
fassia.desc: Enjoy mint tea or Sahrawi Atay with views over the monumental square.

moha.title: Café Restaurant Le Parisien
moha.desc: Popular spot offering European coffee, wood-fired pizzas, and Moroccan dishes.

bacha.title: Foum El Oued Promenade Terrace
bacha.desc: Relaxing oceanfront tables for fresh juices, fried calamari, and sunset tea.

elfenn.title: Street Grill & Sandwiches
elfenn.desc: Casual local market grills serving quick brochettes, kofta, and fresh breads.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.desc: Yellow petit taxis are plentiful and economical within the city. Grand taxis run frequently to El Marsa and Foum El Oued beach.

bargain.title: Weather & Climate
bargain.desc: Enjoyable sunny desert climate year-round with mild Atlantic ocean breezes. Evening temperatures can drop noticeably in winter.

water.title: Sahrawi Etiquette
water.desc: Hospitality is deep-rooted. Accepting tea when offered is customary. Respect local social norms and ask before photographing people.

daytrips.title: Best Day Trips from Laâyoune
daytrips.subtitle: Explore coastal reserves, historic Sahrawi towns, and desert oases.

atlas.title: Tarfaya & Saint-Exupéry
atlas.desc: Historic Aéropostale town and coastal fort about 1 hour north.

agafay.title: Khenifiss National Park
agafay.desc: UNESCO biosphere reserve lagoon for birdwatching and sand dunes.

ouzoud.title: Smara Oasis Town
ouzoud.desc: Historic spiritual desert city inland along the Saguia el-Hamra.

essaouira.title: Boujdour Coast Drive
essaouira.desc: Scenic coastal road driving south with dramatic ocean cliffs.

q1.question: Is Laâyoune easy to reach?
q1.answer: Yes, Hassan I Airport (EUN) offers regular direct domestic flights from Casablanca and Agadir, as well as international connections. The N1 coastal highway connects it smoothly by road.

q2.question: How far is the beach from the city?
q2.answer: Foum El Oued beach and the port of El Marsa are located about 20 to 25 kilometers west of the city center, reachable in 20 minutes by taxi or car.

q3.question: How many days should I spend in Laâyoune?
q3.answer: 2 to 3 days allow you to explore the city squares, enjoy fresh seafood at the port, relax on Foum El Oued beach, and take a dune excursion.

q4.question: What is the best month to visit Laâyoune?
q4.answer: From October to April, the climate is pleasantly warm and sunny, avoiding the intense heat of peak summer.
